560	   * "not yet settling" value and flip isGuestState to false immediately, before mergeBasket.mutate
561	   * has registered anything in the mutation cache. A ref mutation is visible immediately to any
562	   * code running later in the same synchronous effect-flush pass, which is exactly what this
563	   * needs. This is the same class of stale-closure trap useCartMergeAndCap.ts's own docblock
564	   * already documents fixing (a React-render-time value instead of a live read) — applied here to
565	   * the ordering between two different hooks in the same fiber rather than to a single async
566	   * closure.
567	   *
568	   * queryClient.isMutating() (a live, imperative read, taken fresh at the moment this effect body
569	   * runs) — not the reactive `isMutatingSignal` value below — is what actually decides whether to
570	   * flip isGuestState. `isMutatingSignal` (useIsMutating()) exists purely so this effect re-runs
571	   * every time the app-wide mutation count changes, giving it a fresh chance to re-check the live
572	   * value; using its own render-time value directly would reintroduce the identical stale-read
573	   * risk described above. Matches useCartMergeAndCap.ts's own documented reasoning for the same
574	   * hook pairing (queryClient.isMutating() for correctness, useIsMutating() for reactivity).
575	   * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
576	  const { isRegistered } = useCustomerType();
577	  const [isGuestState, setIsGuestState] = useState(!isRegistered);
578	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
579	  const isMutatingSignal = useIsMutating();
580	  const hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef = useRef(false);
581	
582	  // 1:1 Figma-alignment audit fix, 2026-09-22 (Marcel's own direct decision): re-opens the cart
583	  // once a guest's wishlist auth flow succeeds — the counterpart to openGuestWishlistDrawer
584	  // below closing it first. useWishlistAuthDrawer's own sessionStorage fallback (its own
585	  // PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY) already guarantees onAuthSuccess fires here reliably whether
586	  // the shopper authenticated in-page (email code) or via a full-page social-IDP redirect — this
587	  // callback doesn't need to distinguish the two paths itself. No trigger element is passed to
588	  // onOpen: there's no real user click to capture at this exact moment (this fires from an auth
589	  // callback, not a click handler), so the previous trigger — whatever originally opened the
590	  // cart — is left in place as the AC10 focus-return target once the cart finally closes for
591	  // good, per onOpen's own doc ("the previous trigger... is left untouched rather than cleared").
592	  // Once the cart remounts, ZimmCartItemActions/usePendingWishlistItem's own existing mount-time
593	  // sessionStorage check (already built for the redirect case) naturally resumes the pending
594	  // move — nothing new needed there.
595	  //
596	  // Confirmed bug, 2026-09-23 (Marcel's direct report, live-tested): create-account's own
597	  // onAuthSuccess fires as part of the very same event that navigates to /account (see
598	  // REOPEN_AFTER_ACCOUNT_CREATION_DELAY_MS's own doc comment for why) — calling onOpen()
599	  // synchronously here raced that navigation and lost, every time, live-confirmed (the drawer
600	  // stayed closed on /account, though the resumed move itself still completed correctly once
601	  // manually reopened — proving this race, not the resume logic, was the actual gap). Deferred
602	  // by the same short delay this codebase already uses for an analogous settle-then-transition
603	  // case, so the navigation's own pathname-triggered close (useCartDrawer.ts) has already
604	  // resolved before this reopen runs, rather than the two racing in the same tick. Harmless for
605	  // the email-code/social-login paths too: neither navigates away, so this delay just means a
606	  // barely perceptible pause before a reopen that was always going to happen regardless.
607	  const handleAuthSuccess = useCallback(() => {
608	    hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef.current = true;
609	    setTimeout(() => onOpen(), REOPEN_AFTER_ACCOUNT_CREATION_DELAY_MS);
610	  }, [onOpen]);
611	
612	  const wishlistAuthDrawer = useWishlistAuthDrawer({
613	    onAuthSuccess: handleAuthSuccess,
614	    intentId: CART_WISHLIST_INTENT_ID,
615	  });
616	
617	  useEffect(() => {
618	    if (!isRegistered) {
619	      setIsGuestState(true);
620	      return;
621	    }
622	    // Steady-state (a shopper already registered when this container mounts) never sets the ref,
623	    // so `!hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef.current` is true immediately — no artificial wait for
624	    // someone with nothing to wait for.
625	    if (!hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef.current || queryClient.isMutating() === 0) {
626	      hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef.current = false;
627	      setIsGuestState(false);
628	    }
629	  }, [isRegistered, isMutatingSignal, queryClient]);
630	
631	  /**
632	   * Opens the one shared wishlist auth drawer from any row's guest click. ZimmCartItemActions'
633	   * onGuestWishlistClick is `() => void` — no event to forward, because every row shares this one
634	   * drawer instance (ZimmCartItemActions' own docblock explicitly rejects one useWishlistAuthDrawer
635	   * per row). useWishlistAuthDrawer's handleTriggerClick needs a SyntheticEvent purely to capture
636	   * `e.currentTarget` as the AC10 focus-return target.
637	   *
638	   * document.activeElement is deliberately NOT used as a substitute here, even though it could
639	   * plausibly hold the real clicked row's own link at this exact point in the call stack:
640	   * useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's own handleTriggerClick comment already documents exactly why it
641	   * chose `e.currentTarget` over `document.activeElement` for this identical purpose — "unlike
642	   * document.activeElement which may still be body on click." Building this on a mechanism that
643	   * file's own author already rejected for the same job would trade one honest degradation for a
644	   * silently unreliable one.
645	   *
646	   * 1:1 Figma-alignment audit fix, 2026-09-22 (Marcel's own direct report + decision): this used
647	   * to open the auth drawer without closing the cart first, so the two stacked — unmanaged
648	   * DOM/paint order, not a deliberate layering, since both use the same `zIndex: 'modal'`. Now
649	   * closes the cart drawer first (`onClose()`), so the auth drawer opens alone instead. This
650	   * supersedes this comment's own earlier note (removed here) about focus landing on the
651	   * still-open cart drawer's own sentinel on close — the cart isn't still open any more, so that
652	   * particular degradation no longer applies. See `handleAuthSuccess` above for the other half:
653	   * the cart reopens once the auth flow actually succeeds.
654	   */
655	  const openGuestWishlistDrawer = useCallback(() => {
656	    onClose();
657	    wishlistAuthDrawer.handleTriggerClick({ currentTarget: document.body } as unknown as SyntheticEvent<HTMLElement>);
658	  }, [onClose, wishlistAuthDrawer.handleTriggerClick]);

governs unchanged, while a short cart (1-2 items) now gets forced up to the
full available height instead of sizing to its own small content. That

rather than nothing to hide.

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(wishlist-auth-drawer): SFCC-11 persist pending intent when a guest creates a new account

onCreateAccount used to close the drawer and open SFCC's own register modal
without writing anything to the pending-intent store, unlike the email-code
and social sign-in paths, which already persist one before sending the
shopper off to authenticate. A guest who chose to create a new account
(rather than sign in) got their account created fine, but the wishlist add
they originally clicked was silently dropped — nothing was recorded to tell
the app to resume it once isRegistered flipped true.

Now writes the same pending-intent shape the social handlers already use
before opening the register modal, so the existing isRegistered-plus-
matching-intent effect picks it up and fires onAuthSuccess the same way a
social-redirect return already does. No new mechanism, just applied to the
one path that was missing it.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(cart): SFCC-11 defer cart drawer reopen to avoid racing create-account's navigation

Creating a new account navigates to /account as part of the same success
event that fires handleAuthSuccess here — and the drawer's own
[pathname]-keyed close effect (useCartDrawer.ts) reacts to that same
navigation on the same tick. Calling onOpen() synchronously always lost
that race: live-confirmed the drawer stayed closed on /account every time,
though the resumed cart action itself still completed correctly once the
drawer was reopened manually, proving this was a reopen race, not a
resume-logic gap.

Deferring onOpen() by a short delay (matching useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's
own DRAWER_ANIMATION_DELAY_MS pattern) lets the navigation's own close
resolve first, so reopen no longer races it. Harmless for the email-code
and social-login paths, which never navigate away in the first place —
this just adds an imperceptible pause before a reopen that was already
going to happen.
EOF
)"

commit d458a85666e7db90ed71237b0a90e00549ffc282
Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 24 00:50:44 2026 +0800

    fix(cart): SFCC-11 defer cart drawer reopen to avoid racing create-account's navigation
    
    Creating a new account navigates to /account as part of the same success
    event that fires handleAuthSuccess here — and the drawer's own
    [pathname]-keyed close effect (useCartDrawer.ts) reacts to that same
    navigation on the same tick. Calling onOpen() synchronously always lost
    that race: live-confirmed the drawer stayed closed on /account every time,
    though the resumed cart action itself still completed correctly once the
    drawer was reopened manually, proving this was a reopen race, not a
    resume-logic gap.
    
    Deferring onOpen() by a short delay (matching useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's
    own DRAWER_ANIMATION_DELAY_MS pattern) lets the navigation's own close
    resolve first, so reopen no longer races it. Harmless for the email-code
    and social-login paths, which never navigate away in the first place —
    this just adds an imperceptible pause before a reopen that was already
    going to happen.

message.content: let's recap, what's the issue here? ELI5BITFEDLTOP

content.text:
**Consequence:** A guest has items in their cart, logs into an *existing* account (via the header's "My Account" icon). Their guest cart should merge into that account's cart. It doesn't — no error, no sign anything's wrong, they just end up without what they added as a guest.

**Mechanism:** Inside `AuthModal` (now ported to `overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.tsx`), an effect watches for the shopper becoming `isRegistered`. The moment it sees that flip to true, it's supposed to show a "welcome back" toast, merge the baskets, and fire the login-success callback. The flip genuinely happens — a real login correctly writes `"registered"` into localStorage, confirmed directly. But this specific effect, running inside the real composed modal, never sees it — it just keeps reading the old value, forever, even though the component visibly re-renders dozens of times after login. The same hook, tested completely on its own with nothing else around it, reacts to that exact same change correctly. So it's not the mechanism that's broken — it's something about this specific composition.

This isn't a guess — it's a fully automated, reproducible test: real account, real login, no mocks, run twice (once after clearing the build cache and restarting the dev server, to rule out staleness), same result both times. A visual marker also confirmed we were watching the correct component instance the whole session, so it's not a "wrong thing observed" mixup either. What makes this genuinely odd: the React feature this relies on (`useSyncExternalStore`) is specifically built so this *can't* go stale — it's supposed to re-check the real value on every single render, regardless of why that render happened. By React's own contract, what we're seeing shouldn't be possible.

**Fix:** None yet — that's the work ahead of us. Everything done so far was diagnosis: get the file overridden so it could be instrumented, prove the bug is real, rule out the wrong explanations, then strip all the debug scaffolding back out. `use-auth-modal.tsx` is now a clean, behavior-identical port with nothing added yet — waiting for the actual fix. Root cause of *why* this one `useSyncExternalStore` call loses React's freshness guarantee inside this component is still open.

Ready to start digging into that whenever you are.

Is it one of these, or something else you had in mind?

content.text:
Per this component's own decision log (session-notes.md §SFCC-275, cross-checked against SFCC-309's Jira description) — this isn't a bug CodeRabbit newly found, it's a gap the team already knew about and deliberately deferred.

**What it does today (SFCC-275, this component's actual scope):** renders Checkout + Apple Pay + Google Pay for every domestic/hybrid storefront, hides Apple Pay/Google Pay only for global-e regions (HK, ME). That's the *entire* gating job this component was built to own — region-based visibility. Checkout is fully wired; Apple Pay/Google Pay are decorative only, by design, for this ticket.

**Why they're unwired:** there's a base SFCC hook, `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-sf-payments`), that already exists and is already used elsewhere (PDP checks its `pdp` flag). It returns `{pdp, miniCart, cart, checkout}` — real, working per-surface flags, presumably backed by Business Manager config. `cart` and `miniCart` are sitting right there, unused by this component. SFCC-275's own decision log says explicitly: this hook was checked, but wiring it in was "scope this step wasn't asked to add" — that's a separate axis (device/browser eligibility, real payment flows, tokenization) that a resolved scope note assigns to **SFCC-309/383/384**.

**The catch:** those three tickets are explicitly ungroomed — "no ACs, no sprint, unassigned" per that same note. There's even an open question sitting on SFCC-309 that nobody's answered yet: *"confirm which storefronts support G Pay and Apple Pay."* So "expected behavior, fully wired" isn't fully specified anywhere yet — it depends on work that hasn't been scoped.

**Net:** what CodeRabbit flagged is real (buttons render enabled, click does nothing) but it's known, disclosed, deliberate scope-splitting — not something to quietly patch. Per the branch rules, work that depends on an unassigned, ungroomed ticket is a stop-and-ask, not a go-ahead. Your call on what to do with it — leave as-is, add a stopgap disable, or push for SFCC-309 grooming first.

Given the cart contains one or more items with no errors on a domestic storefront, when the cart summary component renders, then the button group displays in the following order: Checkout CTA (primary, full-width black button), Apple Pay Express button (outlined), Google Pay Express button (outlined).

International

Given a Shopper is on an international storefront, when the button group renders, then Apple Pay and Google Pay Express buttons are not displayed and the content above the Checkout CTA shifts up to fill the space with no white gap.

Error States

Given the cart contains an error condition (fully OOS, partially OOS, unavailable item, or quantity error requiring customer action), when the error state renders, then the Checkout CTA, Apple Pay and Google Pay Express buttons remain visually enabled but are blocked at backend level from processing

Given a Shopper resolves all error conditions in the cart, when the last error is resolved, then the Checkout CTA, Apple Pay Express, and Google Pay Express buttons can successfully process — the backend block is removed and the Shopper can proceed

Checkout Routing

Given a Shopper on a domestic storefront clicks the Checkout CTA regardless of authentication status, when the action is triggered, then they are taken directly to checkout.

Given a Guest Shopper on an international storefront clicks the Checkout CTA, when the action is triggered, then they are directed to an intermediate login page before being handed off to Global-e (see SFCC-880).

Given an Authenticated Shopper on an international storefront clicks the Checkout CTA, when the action is triggered, then they are taken directly to the Global-e checkout flow without an intermediate login step (see SFCC-63).

Responsive

Given a Shopper views the button group on any device, when it renders, then all buttons display correctly and are fully interactive across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints in line with Figma specifications.

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the cart drawer's Checkout / Apple Pay / Google Pay button stack (SFCC-275, SFCC-11
 * plan step 5.1). Single style, no parts: all three buttons get their full visual treatment from
 * `ZimmButton`'s own `primary`/`secondary` recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts`) — this recipe only owns
 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});

content.text:
Went through all 8 ACs against the actual code and the team's own resolved notes. Four are met, four aren't — and every one of the four gaps is genuinely blocked, not just unbuilt.

**Met (4):**
- **Default State** — order, primary/full-width/black CTA, outlined icon-only Apple/Google Pay marks. Confirmed in code, and the decision log records a live Figma screenshot check that already caught and fixed one mismatch here.
- **International** — region hide confirmed in code (`checkoutOwner === 'global-e'`). "No white gap" is also confirmed, not just assumed: the recipe deliberately has no fixed `height`/`minHeight`, specifically so a removed child's own space collapses along with it — and there's a regression test asserting that height key stays absent.
- **Checkout Routing #1 (domestic, any auth)** — confirmed: unconditional `navigate('/checkout')`, no auth branch at all.
- **Responsive** — plausible pass (fluid 100%-width flex column, `fullWidth` buttons, nothing breakpoint-specific needed for this layout), but I haven't done an actual cross-device visual check this session — flagging that distinction rather than asserting it outright.

**Lacking, and every one deferred (4):**

| AC | Blocked on |
|---|---|
| Error state — buttons stay enabled, blocked at backend | **SFCC-282** (OOS/partial-OOS) + **SFCC-796** (unavailable) — both real tickets, Hazel's, but Sprint 6, not this one. Plus: "blocked at backend level" is by its own wording a backend/SFCC-side enforcement, not something frontend can build alone regardless of sprint. Zero error-state awareness exists in this component today — not partial, none. |
| Error state — block clears once resolved | Same dependency — it's the release side of the identical not-yet-built mechanism. |
| Checkout routing — guest, international → interstitial | **SFCC-880**: "To Do, unassigned, no sprint." The code is an explicit, self-documented no-op stub, not a hidden gap. |
| Checkout routing — authenticated, international → straight to Global-e | **SFCC-63**/Global-e integration: "Not started," with prerequisite tickets PRC-43/PRC-46 still open. Same stub. |

**Possible-but-simply-not-done: none.** I checked for a middle bucket — something we could just build today without waiting on anything — and there isn't one. Every gap traces to a real, specific, currently-unavailable dependency (an ungroomed/future-sprint ticket, or backend/integration work not started). The one partial exception worth naming: quantity-error detection (`isAtMaxQuantity`) already exists and works today for other purposes, but the AC bundles it with three other conditions that don't have detection yet, and the "visually enabled, backend blocks" mechanism itself doesn't exist in any form — so even that one piece can't ship on its own toward this AC.

Good push — I need to walk back part of my earlier answer. I only checked this component's own recipe in isolation; I hadn't checked how it's actually positioned in the surrounding grid, and that changes the picture.

**What I missed:** `ZimmCartButtonGroup` isn't stacked directly under other content — it sits in **column 2 of a two-column CSS grid** (`ZimmCartDrawer`'s desktop layout), with the items list occupying column 1 as a separate, side-by-side track. Column 2 currently contains *only* the button group's wrapping `Box` — the totals breakdown, promo code, and recommended-for-you sections that Figma shows sharing that same column are explicitly disclosed as out of scope (SFCC-816, not built).

That splits this AC into two genuinely different cases:

- **Tablet/mobile:** the grid collapses to a single stacked flex column, so the items list really does sit above the button group here, in the same vertical flow. I checked this specifically — no fixed heights anywhere in the chain (the recipe, confirmed earlier; the wrapping `Box`'s border/margin/padding are also unconditional, not child-count-dependent) — so the collapse is clean, no dead space. **This case is genuinely met.**
- **Desktop (≥ xl):** column 1 and column 2 are side-by-side grid tracks, not stacked. There is currently nothing else in column 2 above the button group — the content that eventually would be there (totals/promo/recommended-for-you) doesn't exist yet. So on desktop, the AC's own premise — "content above the Checkout CTA" — doesn't correspond to anything built today. It's not that the behavior is broken; there's nothing there yet for a gap to appear against. **Not meaningfully verifiable until SFCC-816 lands.**

So the honest verdict: met for tablet/mobile, not yet testable for desktop — not because this component regressed, but because the AC assumes a more complete column-2 layout than exists right now. Worth flagging as a "can't fully close this AC until SFCC-816" dependency, distinct from the other four gaps we already listed.

content.text:
You're right, and I overcomplicated that. Let me separate what I was actually uncertain about from what's genuinely already done.

**Yes — this is already achieved, full stop.** Both halves:
- **Visibility split:** confirmed in code, region-based, working today.
- **No-gap behavior:** confirmed *mechanism*-level — the recipe has no fixed height/minHeight anywhere in the chain (component + wrapping `Box`), so removing 2 buttons collapses cleanly with nothing to leave a hole. There's an existing test asserting that height key stays absent. That's not "unverified," that's built and proven.

My "not testable on desktop" comment was about a different thing entirely: whether SFCC-816's *future* totals/promo content (which doesn't exist yet) will also collapse cleanly once it's built above the button group in that same column. That's a concern for whoever builds SFCC-816 to get right using this same pattern — it's not a gap in what's here today. I shouldn't have blurred that into this AC's actual verdict. Correcting it: **this AC is met**, not "partially met."

One correction to the framing itself, though, since it matters if you're about to act on it: it's not AU-vs-everyone-else. `checkoutOwner` has three values — `'sfcc'` (domestic) and `'hybrid'` (US) both render all 3 buttons; only `'global-e'` (HK, ME, plus the not-yet-live en-CA/en-CH) hides Apple Pay/Google Pay down to Checkout-only. So it's "non-global-e vs global-e," and US isn't in the checkout-only bucket the way "AU vs the others" would imply.

content.text:
Checked again, and no — it's genuinely not AU vs. everyone else. Domestic (`sfcc`) *and* hybrid (US) both render all 3 buttons; only `global-e` storefronts (HK, ME) drop to Checkout-only. Four independent things all agree on this:

1. The AC text you pasted itself only says "domestic" vs "international" — it never names AU or US specifically.
2. The code: `isInternational = checkoutOwner === 'global-e'` — that's the only condition that hides the express buttons.
3. The component's own decision log explains *why* US groups with AU: `'hybrid'` sites carry `globalEPricing: false`, same as `'sfcc'` sites — every actual `'global-e'` site carries `globalEPricing: true`, and every storefront the design/AC references as the international case (HK, ME) is `'global-e'`, none is `'hybrid'`.
4. There's already a passing regression test asserting this exact thing: `"checkoutOwner 'hybrid' (US) also renders all three, grouped with domestic — see index.tsx decision log item 2."`

If you've got a different source in mind — a PRD line, a Figma note, something from Marcel-the-business-side rather than the code — that's worth surfacing directly, since that would mean the *code* is wrong relative to what was actually asked for, not just my explanation of it. But as it stands, built-and-tested behavior is domestic+hybrid vs. global-e, not AU vs. the rest.

content.text: Now I have Jira and Confluence access — which means I can check the actual requirement sources rather than inferring from code comments. Let me pull all three in parallel.

entries.name: SendUserFile
entries.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

files.description: File paths (absolute or relative to cwd) to send to the user. Always pass an array, even for a single file.

caption.description: Optional short caption for the file(s).

status.description: Use 'proactive' when you're surfacing a file the user hasn't asked for and needs to see now — a generated artifact, a completed report. Use 'normal' when replying to something the user just said.

display.description: How the client should present the file. 'render' opens it inline in the side panel (for HTML, SVG, Mermaid, images, PDFs — anything the user wants to look at now). 'attach' shows a download card only, no inline preview (for deliverables the user will save and open elsewhere). Omit to let the client decide by file type — today that means renderable types render and everything else attaches, same as before this parameter existed.

entries.name: SuggestSkills
entries.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

keywords.description: Topic keywords from the user's request.

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

entries.name: WebSearch
entries.description:
Search the web. Returns result blocks with titles and URLs. US-only.

- The current month is September 2026 — use this when searching for recent information.
- `allowed_domains` / `blocked_domains` filter results.
- After answering from results, end with a "Sources:" list of the URLs you used as markdown links.

query.description: The search query to use

allowed_domains.description: Only include search results from these domains

blocked_domains.description: Never include search results from these domains

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
entries.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

task_id.description: The task_id returned by the spawn_task call that created the chip.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
entries.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

title.description: Short noun-phrase title for the chapter (under 40 chars). Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Optional one-line summary of what this chapter covers. Shown on hover in the table of contents.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__read_widget_context
entries.description: Read context from an embedded interactive widget. Widgets are rendered alongside chat from prior tool calls and can be interacted with by the user. Call this when you need to know the current state of a widget.

tool_name.description: The name of the widget tool to get context for

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
entries.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_click
entries.description: Click an element by CSS selector (e.g., 'button.primary', '#submit', '[data-testid="btn"]').

selector.description: CSS selector for the element to click

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_console_logs
entries.description: Get browser console output (log, info, warn, error, debug). Use to check runtime behavior, debug values, or client-side errors. Use 'level' to filter to errors or warnings only.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_eval
entries.description: Execute JavaScript in the Browser pane's page for DEBUGGING and INSPECTION only. Use for reading page state, DOM queries, checking variables, navigation, page reload, hover/type/key events. Do NOT use this to implement UI changes the user requests — edit the source code instead. Any DOM modifications via eval are temporary and lost on reload. Wrap multi-step logic in an IIFE.

expression.description: JavaScript expression to evaluate in the page context. Return values are serialized as JSON.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_fill
entries.description: Fill an input, textarea, or select element with a value. For select elements, matches by value or text.

selector.description: CSS selector for the input element

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_inspect
entries.description: Inspect a DOM element by CSS selector. Returns text content, className, tagName, id, computed styles, and bounding box. BEST tool for verifying visual properties like colors, fonts, spacing, and dimensions — more accurate than screenshots.

styles.description: CSS properties to return (e.g., ['padding', 'color']). Defaults to common properties.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_list
entries.description: List servers started with preview_start. Returns serverIds for use with other preview_* tools.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_logs
entries.description: Get server stdout/stderr output. Use to check for build errors, verify server behavior, or read debug output. Use 'level' to filter to errors only, or 'search' to filter for specific text. Use after preview_start.

level.description: Filter by level: 'all' (default) shows all output, 'error' shows only lines containing error/exception/failed/fatal

search.description: Filter to lines containing this text (e.g., '[DEBUG]', 'POST /api')

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_network
entries.description: List network requests or inspect a specific response body. Without requestId, lists all requests with URL, method, status, and requestId. With requestId, returns the full response body for that request (useful for inspecting API payloads).

filter.description: Filter: 'all' (default) shows all requests, 'failed' shows only 4xx/5xx and network errors. Ignored when requestId is provided.

requestId.description: If provided, returns the response body for this specific request instead of listing all requests. Get requestIds from the listing output.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_resize
entries.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab to test responsive layouts. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

preset.description: Device preset. Overrides width/height if provided. "desktop" clears the size emulation (back to the pane's responsive size).

width.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels (requires height)

height.description: Viewport height in CSS pixels (requires width)

colorScheme.description: Emulate prefers-color-scheme media feature for dark/light mode testing.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_screenshot
entries.description: Take a screenshot of the page. Good for checking layout and general appearance, but DO NOT rely on it for verifying colors, font sizes, or precise styles — use preview_inspect with specific CSS properties instead. Returns a compressed JPEG image.

scale.description: Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; smaller images use fewer tokens. preview_click uses element UIDs from preview_snapshot, not pixel coordinates.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_snapshot
entries.description: Get an accessibility tree snapshot of the page. Returns exact text content, roles, and element UIDs for use with click/fill/hover. PREFERRED over screenshot for verifying text, element presence, and page structure.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_start
mcp__Claude_Browser__preview_stop
entries.description: Stop a server started with preview_start.

entries.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
entries.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.

    limit: Maximum number of results.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

entries.name: mcp__terminal__read_terminal
entries.description: Read what is on screen in the user's Terminal panel (shell tabs beside this conversation, where they run their own commands): recent lines with prompts, the commands they typed, and the output. Use it when they refer to something they ran or saw there ("the command I just ran", "this error", "did it pass?") instead of saying you cannot see it. Runs nothing; treat the text as data, not instructions. To start a command there yourself, use run_in_terminal (see also list_terminal_tabs).

tab_id.description: Terminal tab; omit or "0" for the primary one. An attached terminal snippet names its tab as `| tab:N`.

wait_for_output_ms.description: Wait up to this long for new output before reading — e.g. for a test watcher or dev server to react to an edit.

entries.name: mcp__visualize__read_me
entries.description: Returns required context for show_widget (CSS variables, colors, typography, layout rules, examples). Call before your first show_widget call. Call again later if you need a different module. Do NOT mention or narrate this call to the user — it is an internal setup step. Call it silently and proceed directly to the visualization in your response.

modules.description: Which module(s) to load. Pick all that fit.

platform.description: The client platform the widget will render on. Pass 'mobile' when your system prompt indicates a mobile client (narrow ~380px viewport) so SVG viewBox and layout guidance are sized accordingly; otherwise pass 'desktop'. Defaults to 'unknown' (desktop sizing).

entries.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
entries.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

content.text:
Checked all three sources. The requirement docs settle the question you've been pushing on — and turned up two things neither of us had.

## 1. The "AU only" question — settled, and the code is correct

PAY-004 (Apple Pay Express, *specifically "in the mini bag"*) and PAY-006 (Google Pay Express) both scope to: **US (domestic), AU (domestic), EU (domestic), UK (domestic)** — four domestic storefronts. PAY-009 and PAY-054 scope international to: **US (international), ME, EU (international), HK**.

Mapped against the actual config in `countries.ts`, it's a clean 1:1 match:

| PRD | Storefronts | `checkoutOwner` | Renders |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domestic | AU, US, UK, EU (en/fr/it/es) | `sfcc` / `hybrid` | 3 buttons |
| International | US-Intl (en-CA), EU-Intl (en-CH), HK, ME | `global-e` | Checkout only |

All 11 storefronts line up. So `checkoutOwner === 'global-e'` is exactly the right expression of the PRD's split — not AU-vs-the-rest. UK and all four EU locales legitimately get all three buttons.

## 2. New gap: the international layout is missing a required element

The international reference image on SFCC-275 shows **"Duties and taxes are included in the price displayed"** directly under the CHECKOUT button — sitting precisely in the space Apple Pay/Google Pay occupy on domestic. That's **PAY-061**: *"display country-specific DDP/DDU messaging on the cart page for applicable countries"* — ALL storefronts, Confirmed.

It's not in the codebase (zero hits for duties/taxes copy), and **no Jira story carries the PAY-061 label** — nor PAY-060, the mini-cart equivalent. Unticketed, unowned requirement.

## 3. The AC's wording is wrong about which content moves

It says content **above** the Checkout CTA shifts up. The reference images show the totals block above the CTA sits in the *same* position in both variants. What actually shifts up is the content **below** — ADD PROMOTION CODE and RECOMMENDED FOR YOU. So the AC names the wrong direction.

## 4. SFCC-275 contradicts itself

The description says: *"The Apple Pay integration, browser detection, and show/hide logic **based on device/browser eligibility or region** are covered in the Payments epic (SFCC-383) — not this story."* But the AC requires exactly that region-based hide. The build followed the AC (right call), but the ticket disclaims what its own AC demands. SFCC-383 ("Apple Pay Express Button (Cart Page & Mini Bag)", holds PAY-004/005) is To Do and **Unassigned**.

**Net on this AC:** the visibility half is implemented, PRD-accurate, and tested. The "no white gap" half has the correct mechanism but can't be observed end-to-end, because everything that would surround it is unbuilt — totals above and promo/recommended below (SFCC-816), plus the DDP line meant to fill that gap (PAY-061, no ticket). Worth raising 2 and 4 in grooming.

content.content:
### SFCC-315 — Drawer (Cart Variation) · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: header `"BAG • [count]"` with right-aligned X / `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` when empty; count updates
dynamically without reload; slides in from the right, right portion on desktop+tablet with a
non-interactive overlaid background, **full screen on mobile**; closes via X, outside click, and
Escape with **focus returned to the trigger**; no loss of page state or scroll position on close;
responsive per Figma.

- Build as a **new organism wrapping `ZimmDrawer`**, not as a modification to the atom and not as an
  override of base `pages/cart`.
- Reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already has `finalFocusRef` (AC7), the overlay, right placement, size variants,
  mobile full-height, and concurrent-instance scroll-lock coordination — all from SFCC-831/926.
- AC3's dynamic count comes free from basket cache invalidation.
- AC8: verify the scroll-lock **restores** position on close rather than merely unlocking.
- **315 owns the empty-state *header text* only.** The empty *body* is SFCC-277's. Clean split.
- 315 is a dependency for SFCC-270, 274, 316, 318, 404 — and **SFCC-316 (Zimmermann Benefits –
  Contentful) is Sprint 5, Ready for Development, assigned to Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz.** Someone else's
  active-sprint card is waiting on this. **Ship 315 first and standalone.**

### SFCC-270 — Cart Item UI Part 1 · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: per line item — image; name to the right of the image; price; selected colour; selected size;
quantity with `+`/`–` either side; multiple items each individually identifiable; Remove and Wishlist
as **underlined text links below the stepper**; on mobile nothing truncated or hidden.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): override base `product-item`.** Cart keeps using it. Separately,
upcoming wishlist work moves the account wishlist page onto `ZimmProductCard` (which already has a
`variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove`), so it stops consuming `product-item` at that point.

Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
```
pages/cart  ->  components/product-item-list  ->  components/product-item
pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
```
Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the
checkout summaries).

**Copy-first scope — 3 files** from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/`:
`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.

**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
8-file one with checkout blast radius.**

**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.

**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): Option B — override `item-variant/*` as well. 8 files.**
`product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}` +

content.content:
1	# PRD – Cart & Inventory
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Cart & Inventory" and "Order Management". Last updated: 2026-06-19.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mini-Cart (CAI-001 – CAI-005)
8	
9	- Opens as an overlay on Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click (CAI-001)
10	- Per line item: product image, name, colour, price (was/now if on sale), size, quantity, item total (CAI-001, CAI-006)
11	- Actions per line item: Move to Wishlist, Remove (CAI-004)
12	- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a mini-cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-004). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
13	- Subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront) with Checkout CTA navigating to checkout entry (CAI-002), and View Bag link to full cart page (CAI-003)
14	- **"Recommended for You" carousel** beneath bag contents — recommendation engine platform TBC (SFCC Einstein vs Athos Commerce), see Open Items (CAI-005)
15	- No recommendations in checkout or order summary — mini-cart and cart only (CFD-021)
16	- International customers (as determined by selected shipping country): Checkout CTA redirects to Global-e checkout
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 2. Cart Page (CAI-006 – CAI-017)
21	
22	- Per line item: image, name, colour, size, price (was/now), quantity controls (increment/decrement — CAI-007), item total
23	- Actions per line item: Remove, Move to Wishlist (CAI-008)
24	- **Move to Wishlist is authenticated-only at launch** — only logged-in customers can move a cart item to wishlist; an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first (CAI-008). Guest wishlist capability is a logged enhancement, not in scope for go-live — see Section 4.
25	- Order summary: item count, subtotal (incl/excl tax per storefront), shipping (TBC at checkout), tax where applicable, grand total in local currency (CAI-009)
26	- Promo code field (CAI-011) and Checkout CTA (CAI-010)
27	- Empty cart message shown when cart is empty (CAI-012)
28	- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) per order — error displayed if exceeded (CAI-017)
29	- Price changes while item is in cart are automatically reflected; no customer notification required (CAI-016)
30	- Sale pricing (was/now) displayed consistently across mini-cart and cart page (CAI-013)
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 3. Cart Persistence (CAI-014 – CAI-015)
35	
36	- **Guest cart:** persisted for **30 days**
37	- **Logged-in cart:** persisted **indefinitely**
38	- **Cart merge on login:** if a guest adds items and then logs in during checkout, carts are merged (CFD-006)
39	- **Separate bag per storefront** — a customer's AU bag and US bag are independent (CRM-170)
40	
41	---
42	
43	## 4. Wishlist (CAI-018, CRM)
44	
45	- Wishlist requires authentication — guests attempting to save are redirected to login (CAI-018)
46	- **Size-level** wishlist; single global wishlist; one size per product
47	- 18-month inactivity cleanup
48	- Shareable via email
49	- Back-in-stock notifications from wishlist items
50	- Guest wishlist (with merge on login) is **out of scope for go-live** — captured in the enhancement log (CAI-018, ENH-039)
51	- **Wishlist hosting platform (SFCC vs Omneo) is being sized, not confirmed** — see Open Items (ENH-038/039). The Move-to-Wishlist login-prompt behaviour (CAI-004/008) is independent of where the wishlist is ultimately stored.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 5. Inventory Display (CAI-024 – CAI-031, OM-021 – OM-032)
56	
57	### Feeds
58	- Daily full inventory feed from NewStore via MuleSoft (CAI-019)
59	- Delta feed via MuleSoft every **15 minutes** (confirmed — CAI-020)
60	- All inventory calls routed through MuleSoft — never SFCC directly to NewStore (CAI-022)
61	- Mulesoft delivers a combined available-to-promise figure aggregating warehouse and eligible boutique stock per region; this aggregate drives browse-level availability states (Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock) (CAI-023). MuleSoft's ability to perform this aggregation is unconfirmed — see Open Items.
62	
63	### Buffer stock
64	- Configurable buffer threshold **per SKU per storefront** in SFCC Business Manager (CAI-024, CAI-025). Applied at SFCC level, not in the feed itself.
65	- Category-level fallback retained; SKU-level takes precedence; thresholds are **not additive**.
66	- Business users can set buffer stock via bulk upload (by category, colour, store view).
67	- **ADD TO BAG** shown when variant stock exceeds buffer threshold (CAI-026)
68	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when stock is above zero but at or below buffer threshold; Add to Bag disabled and back-in-stock capture presented (CAI-027)
69	- **OUT OF STOCK** also shown when variant stock is fully depleted; same disabled state and back-in-stock capture (CAI-028)
70	- Low-stock indicator shown at size level — **no quantity number displayed**; not displayed in mini-cart or cart (CAI-030)
71	- Business users can suppress OOS products from PLP (CAI-031)
72	
73	### General availability vs. boutique stock
74	- General browsing uses a combined (buffered) stock figure
75	- Boutique inventory: real-time call to NewStore via MuleSoft, **no buffer applied**, only triggered when Find in Boutique flyout panel or BOPIS boutique selection screen is opened
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 6. Reservation (CAI-032 – CAI-036)
80	
81	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart
82	- **Hard reservation** only at order placement
83	- Real-time inventory check via NewStore/MuleSoft when customer proceeds from cart → checkout entry; desired behaviour confirmed, but a new MuleSoft flow is required as none currently exists — see Open Items (CAI-034)
84	- If an item is OOS at checkout entry: Checkout CTA is disabled; customer must remove the item. No auto-removal (CAI-035/036)
85	- Cart notifies customer when an item becomes OOS while in cart (CAI-035)
86	
87	---
88
