tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

content.text:
Good questions — I checked rather than assumed. Here's what's actually true.

**Why it exists at all**

It isn't a "redirect on login" rule. It's base SFCC's `withRegistration` pattern — *replay the click the guest originally made, once they've authenticated*:

```jsx
// node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/with-registration/index.jsx:59
<Component {...passThroughProps} onClick={handleClick} />   // guest click → opens auth modal
<AuthModal {...authModal} onLoginSuccess={onClick} />       // after login → runs the original click
```

For the account icon the original click is `onMyAccountClick` → `history.push('/account')` (`_app/index.tsx:351`). So it navigates not because "login means go to account", but because "you clicked My Account, so we finish that for you after sign-in."

The design assumes only one deferred action exists at a time. Here there are two — "go to my account" (the icon) and "add to wishlist" (the PDP) — and the account one wins by destroying the page the other one needs.

**Who made it, and why**

Split answer:

- The *pattern* is base SFCC's, not ours.
- The *line in our code* is mine — `c5f1680f`, this session. `git log -L` confirms it.

Before that commit the account icon was `{isRegistered && isHydrated() ? <Popover> : <IconButtonWithRegistration>}`. The instant `isRegistered` flipped, the ternary swapped branches and destroyed `withRegistration`'s AuthModal — taking its `useEffect([isRegistered])` with it. That effect runs three things: the basket merge, the welcome toast, and `onLoginSuccess`. All three were silently dead. That's why guest cart merge on login never worked.

My fix remounted the modal outside the ternary so the effect could run. That fixed the merge — and revived the toast and the `/account` navigation along with it. I kept `onLoginSuccess` deliberately, to preserve base semantics. I didn't anticipate it would tear a page down mid-flow.

**Does dropping it affect create-account too?**

No — existing-account login only. In our own override (`use-auth-modal.tsx:323-370`, mirroring base):

- `onLoginSuccessProp()` fires only inside `if (loggingIn)` — `currentView === LOGIN_VIEW`
- `onRegistrationSuccess()` fires only inside `if (registering)` — `currentView === REGISTER_VIEW`

And `grep -rn "onRegistrationSuccess" overrides/app/components/` returns nothing — we never wire it. So **create-account already doesn't redirect today.**

That independently corroborates your own earlier test results: you found create-account flows (wishlist and non-wishlist) were fine, and only the existing-account flows broke. Exactly right — create-account never had the redirect, so it never lost the page, so its wishlist resume survived.

**My read:** the strongest argument for dropping it isn't UX preference, it's consistency — right now the same icon behaves two different ways depending on whether you signed in or registered, which is almost certainly unintentional. Merge and welcome toast are in separate branches and stay untouched either way.

The one real cost, stated honestly: the icon is labelled "My Account" even for guests, so base's "take them there after sign-in" reading is defensible. A guest who clicked it wanting their account page would need one more click after signing in.

Want me to make it? It's a one-line change in `rightBar/index.tsx` (Tier 2, already in my working diff), plus updating the test that asserts the current behaviour.

content.text:
I have to correct my previous answer first — I was wrong, and it matters here.

**There are two redirects, not one.** They're both named `onLoginSuccess`, which is how I misread it:

| Path | Mechanism | Opt-out? |
|---|---|---|
| Login (existing account) | `onLoginSuccessProp()` in the `useEffect([isRegistered])` — supplied by the caller; `rightBar` wires it to `onMyAccountClick` | **Yes** — it's a prop, drop it at the call site |
| Create account | local `const onLoginSuccess = () => navigate('/account')` (`use-auth-modal.tsx:212`), called directly at line 257 after `register.mutateAsync()` | **No** — hardcoded inside the hook |

So create-account *does* redirect to `/account`. Both behaviours are inherited from base — base has the identical local function.

**Risk of changing the create-account path**

Higher than the login one, mostly from breadth rather than any failure mode I could find:

- `overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.tsx` is **Tier 2, "Shared Hooks — 5+ consumers", both squads, coordinate before touching** (`protectedFiles.md:84`). The login change touches only `rightBar`.
- It's hardcoded, so removing it changes **every** registration at once — 4 AuthModal call sites: header icon, `_app`, the wishlist drawer's `registerModal`, the cart drawer's `registerModal`.
- **Zero test coverage** — there's no `use-auth-modal.test.tsx` at all, so nothing catches a regression.
- It diverges from base, so it carries forward into every future `retail-react-app` bump.

What lowers the risk more than I expected:

- I checked the obvious failure mode — user stranded somewhere useless after registering. It doesn't apply: `/login` and `/registration` are separate routes with their own pages that don't use AuthModal. All four AuthModal call sites are overlays on top of a real page, so removing the navigation just leaves the user where they already were.
- Two of those four are the *wishlist* register modals, where `onCreateAccount` has just written a pending wishlist intent precisely so the action can resume — the navigation is actively fighting that.

**One thing worth you testing:** this may explain why your create-account flows looked fine. The intent is stashed in sessionStorage, so an instance that survives navigation (header, cart drawer) can still pick it up — but the PDP instance doesn't survive. A create-account wishlist add started *from a PDP* may well fail the same way. I haven't verified that, so treat it as a hypothesis.

**My recommendation:** do them as two separate commits. The login one now — one line, low risk, directly fixes the confirmed unmount. The create-account one as its own change, since it needs the both-squads coordination flag and should be independently revertible.

For create-account you've got two shapes:
- **(a)** delete the hardcoded navigate — nobody redirects on register; consistent with the login change
- **(b)** route it through the already-declared-but-never-wired `onRegistrationSuccess` prop, defaulting to today's behaviour, so only the wishlist call sites opt out — same governance cost, less behaviour change

Which do you want, and shall I start with the login one?

Dropped it at `rightBar/index.tsx:441` — the header account icon's `AuthModal` no longer gets `onLoginSuccess`. That's the one path I'd actually proved. The hardcoded create-account redirect in `use-auth-modal.tsx:213` is untouched.

**Verified live, full chain:**

```
URL after login      : /product/7721XS26A2?color=CHO   ← stayed on the PDP
wishlist add POST    : 200  .../customers/bclXlHlba1wHoRlXtKkqYYlHJH/product-lists/...
wishlist page        : GOLDENTIME RUFFLE SHOULDER BAG, Chocolate, ONE SIZE
```

That screenshot is the real `/account/wishlist` page, and the item matches the PDP the run started on. The list was empty before, so it's this run's add.

It also confirms all three fixes are pulling together: **200 not 404**, against the *registered* customer id — so the round-4 customer-scoping fix is doing its job, and the page now survives long enough for the deferred add to finish.

**Checks:** 22/22 rightBar tests pass; mutation-tested the new guard by putting `onLoginSuccess` back — exactly the one test failed, nothing else. Full suite 1944/1944, `tsc` clean.

**Worth knowing before you test:** the account icon now behaves consistently for both halves — sign in and register both leave you where you were. The tradeoff I flagged stands: a guest who clicks "My Account" *wanting* their account page needs one more click after signing in.

Still unverified and worth a look when you're testing: a create-account wishlist add started **from a PDP**. That path still hits the hardcoded redirect, and the PDP instance doesn't survive navigation — so I'd expect it to fail the same way. Your earlier create-account runs likely passed because the header/cart-drawer instances do survive.

content.text:
Dev server is down, so I can't capture the wire evidence. Could you restart it when you get a chance?

Meanwhile I found a concrete suspect by reading, and it's specific to the wishlist path.

`capBasketQuantities` opens with an app-wide bail-out (`useCartMergeAndCap.ts:194`):

```ts
if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
  return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
}
```

That counts **every** mutation in the app, not just basket ones — the file's own comment says so explicitly ("commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of them"). The wishlist add (`createCustomerProductListItem`) is exactly such a mutation.

So: wishlist path has an extra concurrent mutation the non-wishlist path doesn't. If the wishlist add is in flight when the merge's `onSuccess` calls the cap, **the cap silently skips**. That asymmetry matches your description — wishlist path behaves differently from the login-only path — and it only became reachable once the redirect fix let the wishlist add actually run. Before that it either 404'd instantly or timed out doing nothing.

**But I want to flag honestly where this doesn't fit.** A skipped cap gives you *over*-cap quantities, not higher-of-two. On your original matrix (authed 1/2/3, guest 2/1/2):

- merge correct + cap skipped → **3, 3, 5**
- merge using `higher_quantity` → **2, 2, 3**

Those are different bugs. Your wording points at the second, my suspect predicts the first. I can't reconcile them from reading alone — and notably, my own scripted runs of this scenario *did* show sum-then-cap working (seeded 2+2 → landed on 3), so I can't reproduce higher-of-two from here yet.

**What are the actual quantities you're seeing?** That single data point splits it cleanly — if any line exceeds 3, it's the cap backing off; if every line is the higher of the two, it's the merge mode and I've missed a caller.

Once the server's up I'll capture the full merge URL (to read `productItemMergeMode` directly off the wire), the number of merge calls, and whether the cap PATCH fires or reports `skipped`.

Now I see the constraint: the cart drawer's `handleAuthSuccess` must fire **early** (it sets `hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef` before the gating effect runs). So I can't just reorder `onAuthSuccess` — that would break the cart path that works.

So the wait belongs on the PDP's wishlist add specifically, which is where the proven race is. Adding it as an additive helper in the hook that already owns this domain.

  /**
   * Resolves once no mutation is in flight anywhere in the app, or `false` if that never happens
   * within the bound below.
   *
   * For a caller that wants to fire its own *non-basket* mutation right after sign-in without
   * derailing the merge-then-cap chain. `capBasketQuantities` refuses to run while any mutation
   * is in flight (see its own guard) — and that guard is unscoped by necessity, since
   * commerce-sdk-react's mutation hooks set no `mutationKey`. So an unrelated write landing in
   * the post-merge window makes the cap skip, and the over-cap line survives until something
   * later happens to re-trigger a cap attempt at a quiet moment.
   *
   * Confirmed live (SFCC-11): a guest who adds to wishlist then signs in has
   * `createCustomerProductListItem` in flight across exactly that window — merge request at
   * 30980ms, wishlist-add request at 31279ms, and every cap attempt from 31251ms onward reporting
   * `isMutating: 1` and skipping. The login-only path has no such second mutation, which is why
   * it caps correctly and the wishlist path does not.
   *
   * Deliberately additive: it changes nothing for existing callers, so the already-working
   * login-only merge path is untouched.
   */
  waitForCartWritesToSettle: () => Promise<boolean>;

content.text:
Your reframe was the right call — the fix landed on the wishlist side, and the working path is untouched.

**Root cause:** the resumed wishlist add was firing *into* the merge→cap window. `capBasketQuantities` refuses to run while any mutation is in flight, and that guard is unscoped by necessity (commerce-sdk-react sets no `mutationKey`, which the file's own comment calls out). So the wishlist add — the one extra mutation the login-only path doesn't have — made the cap skip, leaving an over-cap line behind.

Before:
```
30980ms  -> MERGE sent
31279ms  -> WISHLIST-ADD sent      ← lands mid-window
31251ms  :: CAP entry {isMutating: 1} SKIPPED
31472ms  :: CAP entry {isMutating: 1} SKIPPED
→ 7721XS26A2CHOOSFA x4, no cap PATCH
```

After:
```
27694ms  -> MERGE sent
27972ms  -> CAP PATCH sent
28172ms  <- CAP PATCH 200          ← 5 → 3
28243ms  -> WISHLIST-ADD sent      ← now yields until the chain settles
28448ms  <- WISHLIST-ADD 200
```

**The change**, two files, both additive:
- `useCartMergeAndCap.ts` — new `waitForCartWritesToSettle()` (bounded poll, 4s, then proceeds anyway rather than dropping the shopper's action). Existing callers unchanged, so the login-only merge path is byte-for-byte the same behaviour.
- `product-detail/index.tsx` — `handleAddToWishlistSilent` awaits it before mutating. No-op for an ordinary click with nothing in flight.

I deliberately did *not* reorder `onAuthSuccess` in `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, which was my first instinct — the cart drawer's `hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef` depends on it firing early, so that would have broken the cart path that already works.

**Checks:** 3 new tests, mutation-tested (neutered the wait — both behavioural ones fail, nothing else). Full suite 1947/1947, tsc clean. Instrumentation removed, no debug residue.

**One thing I couldn't reproduce, and want to flag rather than paper over:** I never saw higher-of-two. The wire consistently shows `productItemMergeMode=sum_quantities`, one merge call, and true sums (that line went 3 + 2 = 5, not 3). What I *did* reproduce is the over-cap line surviving. If after re-testing you still see the higher value rather than an uncapped sum, that's a different fault than the one I just fixed — send me the actual numbers and I'll chase it.

content.text:
Fixed. The drawer wasn't failing to *reopen* — nothing had ever opened it on a plain sign-in.

**What I found:** the only post-auth opener is `cartDrawerContainer`'s `handleAuthSuccess`, and it fires exclusively from the cart's *wishlist* auth drawer instance. On a plain login that gate is never true, so nothing opened the cart. Previously you didn't notice because sign-in redirected you to `/account`; now you stay put and the merge happens silently with no feedback.

**The fix**, two files:
- `use-auth-modal.tsx` — new optional `onBasketMerged` prop, fired from the merge's `onSuccess` *after* `capBasketQuantities` settles. Sequencing it after the cap is deliberate: otherwise you'd watch an over-cap quantity flash down to its corrected value.
- `rightBar/index.tsx` — wires it to `onMyCartClick`.

It's separate from `onLoginSuccess` on purpose: that fires on every login, this fires only when a merge genuinely ran.

**Verified live, all three cases:**

| Flow | Result |
|---|---|
| Guest cart with items → sign in (no wishlist) | Drawer **opens** with merged cart (`BAG • 21` at +2s) |
| Guest cart **empty** → sign in | Drawer stays closed — no false pop-open on every login |
| Cart → row Wishlist → sign in | Still reopens as before, unaffected |

**Checks:** new wiring test, mutation-tested (removing the prop fails exactly that one test). Full suite 1948/1948, tsc clean.

One note on scope: I wired this on the header account modal only, since that's your flow. The other three `AuthModal` mounts (`_app`, and the wishlist/cart register modals) don't pass it — the wishlist ones already have their own reopen. Say the word if you want it on `_app`'s too.

Nothing committed.

8	import React, {useEffect, useState} from 'react'
9	import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
10	import {useIntl, defineMessage, FormattedMessage} from 'react-intl'
11	import {Box, Container, Heading} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
12	import {
13	    AuthHelpers,
14	    useAuthHelper,
15	    useCustomerBaskets,
16	    useCustomerId,
17	    useCustomerType,
18	    useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation
19	} from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react'
20	import useNavigation from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-navigation'
21	import Seo from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo'
22	import {useForm} from 'react-hook-form'
23	import {useRouteMatch} from 'react-router'
24	import {useLocation} from 'react-router-dom'
25	import useEinstein from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein'
26	import useDataCloud from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-datacloud'
27	import LoginForm from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/login'
28	import OtpAuth from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/otp-auth'
29	import {API_ERROR_MESSAGE} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'
30	import {usePrevious} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-previous'
31	import {isServer, noop} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils'
32	import {
33	    getAuthorizePasswordlessErrorMessage,
34	    getLoginPasswordlessErrorMessage,
35	    getPasswordlessCallbackUrl
36	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/auth-utils'
37	import {getConfig} from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config'
38	import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site'
39	
40	const LOGIN_ERROR_MESSAGE = defineMessage({
41	    defaultMessage: 'Incorrect username or password, please try again.',
42	    id: 'login_page.error.incorrect_username_or_password'
43	})
44	
45	const LOGIN_VIEW = 'login'
46	const EMAIL_VIEW = 'email'
47	
48	const Login = ({initialView = LOGIN_VIEW}) => {
49	    const {formatMessage} = useIntl()
50	    const navigate = useNavigation()
51	    const form = useForm()
52	    const location = useLocation()
53	    const queryParams = new URLSearchParams(location.search)
54	    const {path} = useRouteMatch()
55	    const einstein = useEinstein()
56	    const dataCloud = useDataCloud()
57	    const {isRegistered, customerType} = useCustomerType()
58	    const {locale} = useMultiSite()
59	    const login = useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.LoginRegisteredUserB2C)
60	    const loginPasswordless = useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.LoginPasswordlessUser)
61	    const authorizePasswordlessLogin = useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.AuthorizePasswordless)
62	    const {passwordless = {}, social = {}} = getConfig().app.login || {}
63	    const isPasswordlessEnabled = !!passwordless?.enabled
64	    const passwordlessMode = passwordless?.mode
65	    const passwordlessLoginLandingPath = passwordless?.landingPath
66	
67	    const passwordlessConfigCallback = getPasswordlessCallbackUrl(passwordless?.callbackURI)
68	
69	    const isSocialEnabled = !!social?.enabled
70	    const idps = social?.idps
71	
72	    const customerId = useCustomerId()
73	    const prevAuthType = usePrevious(customerType)
74	    const {data: baskets, isSuccess: isSuccessCustomerBaskets} = useCustomerBaskets(
75	        {parameters: {customerId}},
76	        {enabled: !!customerId && !isServer, keepPreviousData: true}
77	    )
78	    const mergeBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('mergeBasket')
79	    const [redirectPath, setRedirectPath] = useState('')
80	    const [isOtpAuthOpen, setIsOtpAuthOpen] = useState(false)
81	
82	    const handleMergeBasket = () => {
83	        const hasBasketItem = baskets?.baskets?.[0]?.productItems?.length > 0
84	        // we only want to merge basket when the user is logged in as a recurring user
85	        // only recurring users trigger the login mutation, new user triggers register mutation
86	        // this logic needs to stay in this block because this is the only place that tells if a user is a recurring user
87	        // if you change logic here, also change it in login page
88	        const shouldMergeBasket = hasBasketItem && prevAuthType === 'guest'
89	        if (shouldMergeBasket) {
90	            try {
91	                mergeBasket.mutate({
92	                    headers: {
93	                        // This is not required since the request has no body
94	                        // but CommerceAPI throws a '419 - Unsupported Media Type' error if this header is removed.
95	                        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
96	                    },
97	                    parameters: {
98	                        createDestinationBasket: true
99	                    }
100	                })
101	            } catch (e) {
102	                form.setError('global', {
103	                    type: 'manual',
104	                    message: formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE)
105	                })
106	            }
107	        }
108	    }
109	
110	    const handlePasswordlessLogin = async (email) => {
111	        try {
112	            await authorizePasswordlessLogin.mutateAsync({
113	                userid: email,
114	                mode: passwordlessMode,
115	                locale: locale.id,
116	                ...(passwordlessConfigCallback && {callbackURI: passwordlessConfigCallback})
117	            })
118	            setIsOtpAuthOpen(true)
119	        } catch (error) {
120	            const message = formatMessage(getAuthorizePasswordlessErrorMessage(error.message))
121	            form.setError('global', {type: 'manual', message})
122	        }
123	    }
124	
125	    const handleOtpVerification = async (pwdlessLoginToken) => {
126	        try {
127	            await loginPasswordless.mutateAsync({pwdlessLoginToken})
128	            return {success: true}
129	        } catch (e) {
130	            const errorData = await e.response?.json()
131	            const message = formatMessage(getLoginPasswordlessErrorMessage(errorData.message))
132	            return {success: false, error: message}
133	        }
134	    }
135	
136	    const submitForm = async (data) => {
137	        form.clearErrors()
138	
139	        // If passwordless is enabled and the password is not provided, handle passwordless login
140	        if (isPasswordlessEnabled && !data.password) {
141	            const email = data.email
142	            await handlePasswordlessLogin(email)
143	            return
144	        }
145	
146	        try {
147	            await login.mutateAsync({username: data.email, password: data.password})
148	        } catch (error) {
149	            const message = /Unauthorized/i.test(error.message)
150	                ? formatMessage(LOGIN_ERROR_MESSAGE)
151	                : formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE)
152	            form.setError('global', {type: 'manual', message})
153	        }
154	    }
155	
156	    // Handles passwordless login by retrieving the 'token' from the query parameters and
157	    // executing a passwordless login attempt using the token. The process waits for the
158	    // customer baskets to be loaded to guarantee proper basket merging.
159	    useEffect(() => {
160	        if (path.endsWith(passwordlessLoginLandingPath) && isSuccessCustomerBaskets) {
161	            const token = decodeURIComponent(queryParams.get('token'))
162	            if (queryParams.get('redirect_url')) {
163	                setRedirectPath(decodeURIComponent(queryParams.get('redirect_url')))
164	            } else {
165	                setRedirectPath('')
166	            }
167	
168	            handleOtpVerification(token)
169	        }
170	    }, [path, isSuccessCustomerBaskets])
171	
172	    // If customer is registered push to account page and merge the basket
173	    useEffect(() => {
174	        if (isRegistered) {
175	            setIsOtpAuthOpen(false)
176	            handleMergeBasket()
177	            const redirectTo = redirectPath ? redirectPath : '/account'
178	            navigate(redirectTo)
179	        }
180	    }, [isRegistered, redirectPath])
181	
182	    /**************** Einstein ****************/
183	    useEffect(() => {
184	        einstein.sendViewPage(location.pathname)
185	        dataCloud.sendViewPage(location.pathname)
186	    }, [])
187	
188	    return (
189	        <Box data-testid="login-page" bg="gray.50" py={[8, 16]}>
190	            <Heading as="h1" srOnly>
191	                <FormattedMessage defaultMessage="Sign In" id="login.title.sign_in" />
192	            </Heading>
193	            <Seo title="Sign in" description="Customer sign in" />
194	            <Container
195	                paddingTop={16}
196	                width={['100%', '407px']}
197	                bg="white"
198	                paddingBottom={14}
199	                marginTop={8}
200	                marginBottom={8}
201	                borderRadius="base"
202	            >
203	                <LoginForm
204	                    form={form}
205	                    submitForm={submitForm}
206	                    clickCreateAccount={() => navigate('/registration')}
207	                    handlePasswordlessLoginClick={noop}
208	                    handleForgotPasswordClick={() => navigate('/reset-password')}
209	                    isPasswordlessEnabled={isPasswordlessEnabled}
210	                    isSocialEnabled={isSocialEnabled}
211	                    idps={idps}
212	                />
213	                <OtpAuth
214	                    isOpen={isOtpAuthOpen}
215	                    onClose={() => setIsOtpAuthOpen(false)}
216	                    form={form}
217	                    handleSendEmailOtp={handlePasswordlessLogin}
218	                    handleOtpVerification={handleOtpVerification}
219	                    hideCheckoutAsGuestButton={true}
220	                />
221	            </Container>
222	        </Box>
223	    )
224	}
225	
226	Login.getTemplateName = () => 'login'
227	
228	Login.propTypes = {
229	    initialView: PropTypes.oneOf([LOGIN_VIEW, EMAIL_VIEW]),
230	    match: PropTypes.object
231	}
232	
233	export default Login

Copy-first prep done — stopping here for you to verify before I change any behaviour.

**What's in place:**
- `overrides/app/pages/login/index.tsx` — faithful TS port of base's 233-line page. **No functional change yet**: the merge is still base's broken `createDestinationBasket`-only call.
- Temporary marker `console.log('[overrides] pages/login/index.tsx')`, confirmed firing on `/login`.

**Two wiring changes were needed to make the override load at all** (neither touches page behaviour):
- `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — base's `routes.jsx` loads the page via a relative `import('./pages/login')`, which the override resolver never redirects. Without an explicit shadow entry the file was dead code — I verified that directly: the marker didn't fire until I added it. Same trap the file already documents for ProductDetail/ProductList/Confirmation. **This one's Tier 2 (Global Shell)**, so it'll need the code-owner review.
- `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` — added `useRouteMatch`. Base imports it from `react-router`, which ships no types; `react-router-dom` re-exports the identical hook and the repo already maintains its own shim there, so this avoided adding an `@types` dependency.

**Checks:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, full suite 1947/1947.

Could you load `/login` and confirm it behaves normally — form renders, password sign-in works, passwordless/social buttons appear as expected? Once you confirm, I'll remove the marker and make the actual fix: `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'`, route it through `claimBasketMerge` so it can't double-merge alongside the modal, and chain `capBasketQuantities` on success.

One unrelated thing I noticed: most of this session's files are showing as **staged** in `git status` (`M ` in column 1) while `routes.tsx` and `vendor.d.ts` are unstaged. I didn't stage anything — worth a glance before any commit so you get the set you expect.

content.text:
Done. That was the last one.

**The bug:** base's `/login` page merged with no `productItemMergeMode`, so SCAPI applied its `higher_quantity` default — and it never capped at all. Both halves of "the merge and capping" wrong, on a surface that's genuinely reachable: the mobile drawer's Sign In link and the post-signout redirect both land there.

**The fix,** in `overrides/app/pages/login/index.tsx`:
- `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'`
- routed through `claimBasketMerge` so it can't double-merge alongside the modal
- `capBasketQuantities` chained on the merge
- **redirect now awaits the merge** instead of firing in the same tick

That last one turned out to be load-bearing, and I nearly shipped it broken. My first attempt chained the cap on `mutate()`'s `onSuccess` — matching the other two callers. Instrumenting it showed that callback **never fires once**: navigating to `/account` unmounts the page, React Query tears down the mutation observer with it, and the per-call callback is dropped. The cap you'd have seen was an unrelated basket-effect elsewhere noticing the over-cap line later — the same unreliable self-heal that caused the wishlist bug.

Proven by mutation test: with my cap chain deleted entirely, a cap PATCH *still* fired — so the chain wasn't doing the work. After switching to awaited `mutateAsync` → cap → redirect, the page logs `cap result {"status":"corrected"}` from its own call.

**Final wire state:** one merge, `sum_quantities`, merged line `x5` (3 + 2 — a true sum; higher-of-two would be 3), capped to 3.

**Getting the override to load** also needed `overrides/app/routes.tsx` to shadow `/login` — base loads it via a relative import the resolver never redirects, so the file was dead code until then. That's Tier 2 (Global Shell) and will need the code-owner review. Plus `useRouteMatch` added to the existing `vendor.d.ts` shim.

**Checks:** tsc clean, 1947/1947. No test file for this page — `pages/` test precedent exists (`categoryPath`, `recentlyViewed`), so I can add one covering the merge params and the await-before-redirect ordering if you want that before the PR.

Still nothing committed, and the staged/unstaged split I flagged earlier is worth a look first.

content.text:
That's the divergence. The wishlist drawer offers **no password sign-in at all**:

```
buttons: ["Send code", "Sign in with Apple", "Sign in with Google", "Create an account"]
```

So signing into an existing account from this flow means **Send code** (email OTP). I've been signing in via the header account icon with a password — which is why my traces keep coming out clean.

That's not a cosmetic difference. It changes *which caller does the merge*:

| | Path you're on (OTP) | Path I've been testing (password modal) |
|---|---|---|
| Merge caller | `useWishlistAuthDrawer` | `use-auth-modal` |
| Gate that opens | `isOtpAuthOpen` | modal `isOpen` |
| Claim winner | drawer | auth-modal (`wishlist-drawer wonClaim: false`) |

My trace proves `use-auth-modal` is the one merging and capping correctly. **`useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s own merge path has never actually executed in any test I've run** — the claim lock hands it to the modal every time. It's untested code, and it still uses the per-call `onSuccess` shape I just proved can be silently dropped on the login page.

I can't drive OTP myself — it needs the emailed code. So I've left the `[CMP]` tracing in place.

Could you run it once: PDP → Add to Wishlist → **Send code** → enter the code, with DevTools console open, and paste the `[CMP]` lines? That'll show me directly whether the drawer wins the claim, whether its `merge onSuccess FIRED`, and what `cap result` says — the same three facts that cracked the login page.

If you'd rather not, my fallback is to harden that caller the way I did the login page (awaited `mutateAsync` → cap, rather than a droppable `onSuccess`) — but I'd be fixing on inference instead of evidence, and I've been wrong twice this session doing that.

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(cart): SFCC-11 use sum_quantities and cap on every sign-in surface

Signing in with a guest basket kept the higher of the two quantities
instead of the sum, and never applied the per-SKU cap, on every surface
except the header account icon.

The root cause was four base-path imports of use-auth-modal from inside
overrides/. Those silently resolve to the base module in the real app
build, so the wishlist drawer's register modal, _app's modal and the cart
drawer's modal all ran base's merge. Confirmed on the wire: the merge went
out with productItemMergeMode absent and a 3+2 basket came back as 3, with
no cap request at all.

Also in this change:

- claimBasketMerge stops two callers issuing a merge for the same sign-in,
  which previously 409'd the loser and could make the winner's cap back off
- the /login page is now overridden. Base merged there with the same
  defaults, and its redirect fired in the same tick as the merge, so the
  page unmounted before React Query could invoke the per-call onSuccess the
  cap was chained to. The redirect now awaits merge-then-cap
- the header account modal no longer replays its own click as an /account
  redirect on sign-in. That navigation unmounted the PDP 34ms into the
  deferred wishlist add and orphaned it
- useWishlistReady waits for the signed-in customer's own wishlist, so a
  resumed add can no longer target the guest's list and 404
- the resumed wishlist add yields until basket writes settle, so it stops
  tripping the cap's in-flight guard and skipping the correction

Verified live against the dev API on each path: one merge, sum_quantities,
and the over-cap line corrected to its max.
EOF
)" && echo "=== committed ===" && git log --oneline -1

content.text:
Committed as `39617df4` — 23 files, including the four `.claude/registry/*.md` files the pre-commit hook regenerated for the new login page and route. Hook ran the related Vitest files and passed.

**The actual bug, in one line:** four files imported `use-auth-modal` via the base path from inside `overrides/`, which silently resolves to base's module in the real build. So the wishlist drawer's register modal, `_app`'s modal and the cart drawer's modal were all running base's merge — no `sum_quantities`, no cap. `rightBar` used the alias, which is the only reason the header icon path ever worked, and why I couldn't reproduce your failure for so long.

Your reframe is what got there: once you said the two paths should be identical, tracing both side by side showed neither of my instrumented callers logging at all on the broken one — which only makes sense if the code running wasn't ours.

**Before → after on your path** (wishlist → Create an account → Sign in):

```
mode=ABSENT          →  mode=sum_quantities
merged x3 (higher)   →  merged x5, capped to 3
no CAP PATCH         →  CAP PATCH 200
```

Also folded in: the `claimBasketMerge` lock, the `/login` page override (base merged wrong there too, and its redirect fired before the merge resolved so the cap was dead code), removal of the `/account` redirect that was unmounting the PDP mid-add, `useWishlistReady`, and the wishlist add yielding until basket writes settle.

Checks: tsc clean, 1947/1947, verified live on each path.

Two things outstanding:
- **No CodeRabbit review** — you opted out, so that check lands at PR time instead.
- `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-header.tsx` is still uncommitted. Untouched all session, deliberately excluded — it's yours to deal with.

Worth flagging for the PR: `_app/index.tsx` and `routes.tsx` are Tier 2 (Global Shell), so this needs a code-owner review. And the base-path import trap is a landmine for any future override — a `no-restricted-imports` ESLint rule would make it impossible to reintroduce, if you want me to add one.

standalone** because SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint) depends on it. Cart PRs currently get **no
PR-time E2E** — `qa.yml` has no `cart` area, so they resolve to `e2e_scope: skip`.

**Reading lesson worth keeping:** a `see SFCC-NNN` or "Relates to" inside an AC usually points at
where the design or detail lives, **not** at a gate. Treat it as a dependency only when the card
says so outright. I wrongly called SFCC-271, SFCC-275 and one of SFCC-272's ACs blocked on that
basis and had to correct each.

**How to apply:** before planning any further cart story, read `.claude/session-notes.md` first.

content.text:
Here's the accurate picture — I checked the code rather than recapping from memory.

**What we're trying to do:** retire `/cart` as a page. The drawer becomes the only way to view cart contents, and everything that previously linked to `/cart` opens the drawer instead. That's SFCC-315 and its follow-ons (the seven-story Cart bundle in `.claude/session-notes.md`).

**What's implemented and committed:**
- The drawer itself — `zimmCartDrawer`, `cartDrawerContainer`, `zimmCartEmptyState`, `zimmCartItemActions`, `zimmCartButtonGroup`, `cartItemMapper`, and the `useCartDrawer` provider
- Our own surfaces open the drawer: the bag icon routes through `_app`'s `cartDrawer.onOpen`, and PDP/PLP add-to-bag opens it
- This session's merge/cap/wishlist-resume fixes on top

**What's pending — one concrete blocker, and it's the same trap we just fixed twice:**

`overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-header.tsx` is written and sitting uncommitted. It replaces checkout's "Back to cart" link with a drawer open. But it is **dead code**:

```
overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:63
import CheckoutHeader from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/checkout-header';
```

Base path, from inside `overrides/` — so base's version renders and checkout's "Back to cart" still navigates to `/cart`. Third instance of exactly the bug that caused the merge/cap failure. Fix is one line, same as the others.

**Two loose ends beyond that:**
- `/cart` is still a live inherited route — the registry confirms `Inherited`, and it renders base's cart page. I hit it repeatedly in testing this session (`Cart (21 items)`). So the comment in that override claiming the drawer is "the only way to view cart contents sitewide" isn't true yet.
- `recommended-products/index.tsx:252` still branches on `pathname.endsWith('/cart')` — behaviour pinned to a page we're retiring.

**The decision I need from you** is what the end state for the `/cart` route actually is. The session notes say 315 was explicitly *not* to override base `pages/cart`, and they never record a decision about the route itself — only that the drawer "replaces" the page. So: do we drop the route, redirect it, or leave it inherited and just fix the consumers?

content: We're retiring the /cart page so the drawer is the only cart view. The checkout "Back to cart" override is written but dead code, because _app imports the base path instead of ours. Next: decide whether /cart stays a route, gets redirected, or is dropped.

Complete inventory. `/cart` is still a live inherited route (base `routes.jsx:105`, not excluded from our spread), and here's everything that reaches it.

**Live — a shopper can land on `/cart` today:**

| # | Source | Trigger | Override status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-header.jsx:39` — `href="/cart"` | "Back to cart" in checkout | Override **written but dead** — `_app/index.tsx:63` imports it via the base path |
| 2 | `components/order-summary/index.jsx:110` — `<Button as={Link} to="/cart">` | "Edit cart" in checkout's order summary | Not overridden (Tier 2, listed in protectedFiles but no file exists) |
| 3 | `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-checkout-header.jsx:39` — `href="/cart"` | One-click checkout header | Not overridden |
| 4 | `components/bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx:195, 230` — `navigate('/cart','push')` | Bonus/promo product flows | Not overridden; mounted via `BonusProductSelectionModalProvider` |

**Rendered but unreachable — no action needed unless something changes:**

| # | Source | Why it can't fire |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | `hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:471, 548` — "View Cart" → `/cart` | `<AddToCartModal/>` mounts unconditionally, but its only opener is base `product-view`, which we override and which now uses `useCartDrawer()` |
| 6 | `components/sf-payments-express-buttons/index.jsx:326, 951` — `navigate('/cart')` | Guarded by `usage !== EXPRESS_BUY_NOW`; our sole call site (`product-view:971`) always passes `EXPRESS_BUY_NOW` |

**Already converted:** the header bag icon — `_app/index.tsx:336` opens the drawer where base `_app/index.jsx:289` did `buildUrl('/cart')`.

**Non-navigating references** (won't take you there, but are pinned to the page existing): `ssr/contentSecurityPolicy.ts:51` lists `/cart` in the strict-CSP prefixes, and `recommended-products/index.tsx:252` branches on `pathname.endsWith('/cart')`.

Worth noting the drawer's Apple/Google Pay buttons are ours (`zimmCartButtonGroup`), not base's express component — which is why #6 stays dead.

So the real remaining work is items 1–4, and #1 is the one-line import fix we already know about. Items 2–4 need a decision: override each to open the drawer, or drop the route and let them 404/redirect.

name: project-override-import-resolution
description: "Base-path imports from inside overrides/ resolve to the BASE module, not your override — overrideStyling.md claims otherwise"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: bad4ca0d-db64-47ee-b18c-8601052cd7b0
  modified: 2026-09-24T06:55:54.904Z
---

Verified live on 2026-09-24 (SFCC-11, dev server + Playwright marker test), in the **real app
build**, not just Storybook/Vitest:

- From a file under `overrides/`, importing `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal`
  resolves to the **base `.js`** — the override is NOT used (0 debug markers).
- Importing `app/hooks/use-auth-modal` (the `app/` alias) resolves to the **override `.tsx`**
  (12 markers).
- The ccExtensibility resolver does rewrite base-path imports made from **inside the base
  package** — that's how `withRegistration` (in `node_modules`) picked up our override.

**Why:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` ("Importing an already-overridden component from a new
component") states a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app" and that the
problem is confined to Storybook/Vitest. That is wrong about the app build — it runs, but it runs the
*base* version. A fix written into an override silently does nothing for our own components.

**How to apply:** In any file under `overrides/`, import an already-overridden module via the `app/`
alias or a relative path, never the SFCC base path. A base-path import also fails to *parse* under
Vitest when the base file is JSX-in-`.js` (e.g. `use-auth-modal.js`), which is the usual first
symptom. Known consumers still on the base path and therefore silently using the base hook:
`_app/index.tsx`, `pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`,
`ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`, `hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`.
The rule doc itself needs correcting. Related: [[project-styling-layer-boundary]],
[[project-shared-ui-barrel-trap]].

content.text:
That also tells me the **proven pattern** for this exact situation, which answers your question technically.

The regular `Header` is *also* outside the provider — it works because `_app` passes it `onMyCartClick={onCartClick}`, a callback closing over `cartDrawer` directly (`_app` mounts the provider, so it can't consume its own context). So the established method here is **a prop from `_app`**, not `useCartDrawer()` inside the header. Our override reached for the hook instead, which is why it's inert. Fixing it to match `Header` needs no provider hoisting.

On where to send the user — my recommendation is **open the drawer in place, stay on `/checkout`**:

- It's what a drawer is for: an overlay, no navigation, no lost checkout progress
- It matches the site-wide bag icon's existing behaviour
- "Back to cart" stops being a navigation and becomes "review your bag" — which is what it now means once the page is gone

The alternatives, for completeness: navigate somewhere (home/PLP) and open it there, which yanks the shopper out of checkout for no benefit; or drop both controls entirely, since checkout's order summary already lists the items — cleanest structurally, but removes an affordance shoppers look for.

**One caveat I don't want to gloss over:** editing quantities from within checkout can invalidate work the shopper has already done — shipping method and payment are selected against a basket total. I haven't verified how SFCC's checkout reacts to a basket mutation mid-flow. If it doesn't recalculate cleanly, "open in place" could leave checkout in a stale state, and option C (remove the controls) becomes more attractive.

So: do you want **A — open in place on checkout** for both "Back to cart" and "Edit cart"? And if so, shall I verify the mid-checkout basket-edit behaviour first, since that's the one thing that could undermine it?

Note "Edit cart" lives in base `components/order-summary` (Tier 2, not overridden), so that one needs a new copy-first override regardless of which option you pick.

content.text:
Verified. Two findings, one of which changes the recommendation.

**1. Quantity edits mid-checkout are safe.** Changed 2 → 1 with contact, address *and* shipping method (Express/DHL) already completed:

```
before:  Subtotal A$1,790.00   Order Total A$1,790.00
after:   Subtotal A$895.00     Order Total A$895.00
```

All completed steps survived, no errors, totals recalculated correctly. Server side copes cleanly.

**2. Removing the last item is an unguarded dead-end.** The screenshot is the proof — the shopper sits on `/checkout` with:

- `0 items in cart`, Subtotal **A$0.00**, Order Total **A$0.00**
- Contact Info, Shipping Address and Shipping & Gift Options all still showing as complete
- **Payment step open and ready**
- No redirect, no empty-cart message, no guard anywhere

You can reach Payment with an empty basket. Base has no protection for this.

Worth being precise about blame: this is a **pre-existing** hole, not one the drawer creates — you can already hit it by emptying your cart in another tab, or via the `/cart` page, and returning. Putting the drawer on checkout doesn't cause it; it makes it trivially easy to hit, because the drawer offers Remove right there.

**One thing I could not prove:** whether a drawer edit propagates to checkout live, without a reload. My mutation went straight to the API, bypassing React Query, so checkout showed stale totals until I reloaded. The drawer mutates *through* React Query and invalidates the basket query checkout reads, so it almost certainly does propagate — but I can't demonstrate it until the drawer is actually reachable there. Flagging it rather than assuming.

**So my recommendation becomes: A, but conditional.** Opening the drawer in place is right for quantity edits, and it needs an empty-basket guard on checkout to go with it — redirect out (home, or wherever you'd want) once the basket hits zero. That's a genuine extra piece of scope, and arguably its own ticket since the hole predates this work.

Do you want the guard in scope here, or filed separately and we ship the drawer-on-checkout without it?

content.text:
None of the seven is cart work. Six are findings from the audit you asked for; one is leftover WIP. Here's each, then my read.

---

**1. Analytics going to a dead address** — `_app`, `product-detail`, `product-list`, `use-active-data.ts`

*What breaks:* Salesforce's shopper-tracking ("this person viewed that product") is being sent to a web address that isn't the one this site uses. That data most likely never arrives.

*Why:* Someone on the team already noticed and wrote a corrected copy of the tracking code pointing at the right address. But the three pages that use it ask for it by Salesforce's name — and asking by that name quietly hands back Salesforce's original, not ours. So the correction has never once run.

*The change:* point those three pages at our copy. The fourth file is a small type adjustment needed to let our copy accept a product category that hasn't finished loading yet — which it already handled safely.

**2. Product page switches layout at the wrong screen width** — `product-view`

*What breaks:* On a product page at tablet widths (roughly 768–992px), the shopper gets the phone layout when they should get the desktop one.

*Why:* Same trap. We have our own show-on-phone / show-on-desktop helpers that switch over at our breakpoint; the product page asks Salesforce for theirs, which switch over at a wider one.

*The change:* point it at ours.

**3. A door that leads to the wrong room** — `list-menu/index.ts`

*What breaks:* Nothing today.

*Why:* That folder has a "front door" file listing what's inside. It was handing out Salesforce's plain 80-line menu instead of our 282-line mega-menu. Nothing goes through that door right now — the menu reaches our file directly — so no one has hit it.

*The change:* fix the door, so the next person through it doesn't silently get the wrong menu.

**4. Leftover WIP** — `checkout-header.tsx` (untracked)

Only ever existed to turn "Back to cart" into a drawer. That button isn't in Zimmermann's checkout, so it has no reason to exist.

---

**My read — discard all seven from this branch.**

Not because they're wrong. #1 and #2 are real, and I'd want them fixed. But:

- None belongs to the cart story this branch tells
- Neither #1 nor #2 is verified live — I proved the *mechanism*, not these specific behaviours
- #2 shifts a visible breakpoint on the PDP with no design eye on it
- #1 sits in the Einstein/Active Data domain, which per our own notes is already blocked (Einstein shows "Not Deployed" across all eight sites, DNT defaults on) — so fixing the address may change nothing observable while touching a stream someone else owns
- #3 is free, but it's one line and equally happy in its own ticket

So: file #1, #2, #3 as tickets, delete #4. The real deliverable from this detour is the audit itself — it found four dead overrides, three of which we'd been treating as working.

Say the word and I'll revert the six and draft the tickets. Or if you'd rather keep #3 since it's risk-free, that's a reasonable line to draw too.

The audit didn't leave code behind, but it did leave knowledge worth keeping:

- **Four dead overrides found** — `checkout-header`, `components/responsive`, `use-active-data`, and `list-menu`'s barrel. Three of those we'd been treating as working.
- **The rule:** inside `overrides/`, a `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` import hands back the *base* module. Correct when a file extends its own base; silently wrong when it reaches for a different module we've overridden. This is already recorded in memory and live-verified — and it's what caused the merge/cap bug we spent most of today on.
- **The audit is repeatable** — the script is in the scratchpad and runs in seconds against the whole tree.

Worth a ticket each for the three real bugs, plus a correction to that rule doc. I can draft them whenever you want — and the ESLint `no-restricted-imports` guard would make the whole class unrepeatable.

---

Verified 2026-08-25 against the live Contentful API (read-only CDA + CMA). **Re-checked
2026-08-27: dev has grown to 19 content types, code now defines 6 — see the updated gap
below.**

**Tier state (updated 2026-08-27):** content HAS now been promoted out of dev — `dev` has 19
content types / 47 published entries (49 via preview, so 2 drafts), and `test`, `sit`, `uat`
each have **38 entries**. `staging` is still **0 entries** and `prod` still has no
`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` or delivery token. The 25 Aug reading below (all non-dev tiers at
zero) is superseded — do not quote it as current.

Consequence for staging/prod: every `useUiCopy` key silently renders its hardcoded English
fallback there, with no error surfaced anywhere. Verified by pointing the uiCopy check at
`staging` — all 5 call-site keys reported missing.

**Two separate mechanisms.** Content *types* promote via an org-scoped Environment Template
(`sync:contentful` builds it, `install:contentful --target` installs it). Entries **cannot**
travel that way — it's structural: `EnvironmentTemplateProps.entities` has exactly
`contentTypeTemplates` and `editorInterfaceTemplates`, no entry slot. The only entry-writing
code in the repo is `seedRegions.mjs:71-72` (11 `region` entries, that's all).

**As of 2026-08-27 the gap is 6-in-code vs 19-live.** Code on `develop` defines
`footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `image`, `link`, `region`, `uiCopy`. Dev gained six types
since the 25 Aug sweep (`gallery`, `galleryItem`, `headerNavItem`, `headerNavigation`,
`imageAndText`, `navGroup` — header/gallery work in flight), and **`footerNavGroup` is
defined in code but no longer live in dev** (apparently superseded by `navGroup`), so drift
now runs in both directions. 14 live types have no code definition at all. Historical
snapshot from 25 Aug follows.

**The template covers 5 of dev's then-14 types** — `footerConfig`, `footerNavGroup`, `link`,
`region`, `uiCopy`. The other 9 (`collectionPageExp`, `contentCard`, `homepageContentRow`,
`homepageHeroBanner`, `image`, `pdpAccordionContent`, `plpInlineGridInsert`, `product`,
`promotionalAnnouncementBanner`) exist only inside the dev environment, UI-authored, with no
code representation.

**There is no forward content promotion at all.** The repo's actual release model is the
alias flip in `promoteAlias.mjs`: clone master → install template → author/verify → repoint
`production`/`master`. Content moves backwards (master → clone), never forwards.

**Why:** this took a full multi-agent investigation to establish and none of it is visible
from the repo alone — the tier state is live external state, and the 5-vs-14 gap only shows
up by diffing `content-types/*.js` against the live CDA.

**How to apply:** before promising any content-related fix on a non-dev tier, check whether
that tier has the content model at all. Don't assume `install:contentful` moves content — it
moves schema, and only the 5 types in `content-types/`. See [[project-contentful-known-bugs]].


---

**CORRECTED 2026-09-22 (live CDA check).** Entry counts above were wrong — "~38 across
test/sit/uat" is true of **uat only**:

| env | entries | types |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dev | 148 | 14 |
| test | 100 | 10 |
| sit | 97 | 9 |
| uat | 38 | 6 |
| staging | 0 | 6 |
| prod | uncheckable — `.env.prod` has no `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | — |

Code defines **10** content types (`scripts/contentful/content-types/`, 457 lines total,
23–76 lines each). dev carries 4 extras not in code: `collectionPageExp`, `richtext`,
`sizeGuide`, `sizeGuideTable`; sit has a stray `zimmermann`.

**Promotion debt:** staging and uat still carry the pre-unification `footerNavGroup` — they
never received the `navGroup` unification (`d934ad96`, 2026-08-26) and are ~1 month behind
the template. Installing any new content type there is not a clean run today.

content.text:
Checked live against the CDA rather than quoting the note — which turned out to be stale.

**What's Contentful-driven in the cart build**

Three things:
- **`ZimmBenefits`** — the "Zimmermann Benefits" block (Free Returns / Fast Shipping / Secure Payments) in the drawer footer. Fetches an `iconAndText` entry filtered on `fields.placement=benefits`. Rendered by `cartDrawerContainer` only when `itemCount > 0`.
- **`cartDrawerContainer`** and **`zimmCartEmptyState`** — microcopy via `useUiCopy`.
- Content types `iconAndText` + `iconAndTextItem` are defined in code. Code now defines 12 types total; the memory note said 10, and those two additions are precisely the cart's.

**Status per tier — live, today**

```
tier      | types | entries | iconAndText | placement=benefits | uiCopy
----------+-------+---------+-------------+--------------------+-------
dev       | 14    | 163     | 1           | 1                  | 37
test      | 14    | 167     | 2           | 2  <- duplicate    | 37
sit       | 13    | 163     | 1           | 1                  | 37
uat       |  6    |  38     | 400 absent  | 400 absent         |  5
staging   |  6    |   0     | 400 absent  | 400 absent         |  0
prod      | no delivery token and no environment id in .env.prod
```

**Three problems worth your attention:**

**1. uat and staging can't render the benefits block at all.** They're still on the old 6-type model — `iconAndText` doesn't exist there, so the CDA 400s. `ZimmBenefits` returns `null` on missing data, so the block just silently isn't there. No error, no warning. Same for microcopy: staging has zero entries, uat has 5 of 37, so `useUiCopy` quietly serves hardcoded English. Per the earlier record these two haven't moved in three days.

**2. `test` has two published `placement=benefits` entries.** The component does `entries?.[0]`, so which one renders isn't deterministic. Whoever QAs the drawer on test could be looking at either.

**3. prod has no Contentful configuration whatsoever** — no delivery token, no environment id. Anything Contentful-driven, including this benefits block, has nowhere to read from. That's a go-live blocker, not a cart-specific one.

**One thing to reconcile:** the cart decision record calls SFCC-316 "Zimmermann Benefits – Contentful" (Jhoan, Sprint 5), but the component's own docblock cites SFCC-317, and describes its placement as provisional — "Shipping & Returns PDP drawer tab (until cart drawer ships — SFCC-825/277)". It's now in the cart drawer, so either that comment is stale or the placement decision moved without the comment following. Worth a look before anyone trusts either ticket number.

I've refreshed the memory note with the verified table.

content.text:
Short answer: **yes for dev/test/sit, no for uat/staging/prod.**

The cart's Contentful surface is narrower than it might look — I checked what the code actually asks for, not what the tickets imply:

| What the cart needs | Source |
|---|---|
| Zimmermann Benefits block (drawer footer, `itemCount > 0`) | `iconAndText` entry, `fields.placement=benefits` |
| `cart.item.alreadyInWishlist` | `uiCopy` |
| `cart.item.maxQuantityReached` | `uiCopy` |

Everything else in the cart is **not** Contentful. The empty state (`zimmCartEmptyState`) uses `react-intl` `defaultMessage`, so its copy lives in translation files. The button group, quantity stepper, item actions and drawer chrome carry no Contentful dependency at all.

**Per tier:**

```
tier      | benefits entry | cart.item.alreadyInWishlist | cart.item.maxQuantityReached
----------+----------------+-----------------------------+------------------------------
dev       | 1              | PRESENT                     | PRESENT
test      | 2  <- dupe     | PRESENT                     | PRESENT
sit       | 1              | PRESENT                     | PRESENT
uat       | type absent    | MISSING                     | MISSING
staging   | type absent    | MISSING                     | MISSING
prod      | no Contentful credentials at all
```

So: **dev, test and sit have everything the cart build needs.** You can build and QA against those with complete content.

**uat and staging have none of it** — they're still on the old 6-type model, so `iconAndText` doesn't even exist there, and neither uiCopy key is present. The failure is entirely silent: the benefits block renders `null`, and the two messages fall back to hardcoded English. Nothing errors, nothing logs. A tester on uat would see a cart drawer that looks finished and simply has no benefits panel.

**prod has no Contentful configuration whatsoever** — no delivery token, no environment id.

Two caveats on the "yes":

- **test has two published `placement=benefits` entries.** The component takes `entries[0]`, so which renders isn't deterministic. Someone should delete the duplicate before it confuses QA.
- I've verified what the *current code* requests. If any of the seven cart stories specifies content that hasn't been built yet, it wouldn't show up in this sweep — the decision record only mentions Contentful for the benefits block (SFCC-316/317). Worth a glance at the remaining cards' ACs if you want that fully closed off.

Audit the mega cart build for race conditions. READ ONLY — do not edit any file.

Scope (read all of these fully):

- waitForWishlistReady resolving with the guest's list -> customer-scoped reset during render
- Base-path use-auth-modal imports resolving to base

- The unmount-orphaned callback class I proved today: mutate(vars, {onSuccess}) never fires if the owning component unmounts first. Any other call site with that shape?

- Rapid repeated clicks (quantity stepper, remove, wishlist) issuing overlapping mutations
- Effect ordering across separate component trees reacting to the same auth/basket transition
- Optimistic updates vs server truth

For each finding report: file:line, the concrete sequence that triggers it, the user-visible consequence, and your confidence (CONFIRMED by reading the code path end-to-end, vs PLAUSIBLE). <result>Audited the cart build for race conditions, read-only. Five findings, none of them the four already fixed.

**1. CONFIRMED — post-auth wishlist move silently lost.** `usePendingWishlistItem.ts:152` keys its effect on `[isGuest]` alone, and clears both stores (:145-146) *before* calling `onResume()` (:150). That resolves to `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:706 moveToWishlist`, which reads `wishlist?.id` from `useWishList()` (:674) with no wait and returns `{status:'error'}` at :715-721 when it's absent.

Sequence: guest clicks Wishlist on a cart line → authenticates → `isGuest` flips false → effect fires in that same commit → `useWishList()` has just re-keyed to the new customerId, so `wishlist` is `undefined` → error branch → `ZimmCartItemActions` deliberately emits nothing for `'error'` (:120-122). No toast, item not removed, intent already cleared, and the effect won't re-run because `wishlist` isn't a dependency.

This is the exact defect class fixed in `product-detail` with `useWishlistReady`. The cart path never received that fix, and it breaks the cart's headline guest→sign-in flow.

**2. CONFIRMED — stale `onResume` closure.** Same `[isGuest]`-only effect. `attemptMoveToWishlist` is a `useCallback` over `onMoveToWishlist`/`onRemove`, which are fresh arrows every container render (:368-369). The effect captures whichever closure existed when it last ran, so a resumed move can target an older render's `basket.basketId`/`wishlist`. Compounds #1.

**3. CONFIRMED — cap correction dropped until the next basket change.** `useCartMergeAndCap.ts:231` returns `skipped` *before* the version-key write, so a retry is permitted — but the only retry driver is `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:547-554`'s `[basket]` effect. If the skip lands on the final basket state, nothing re-triggers it and the over-cap line persists until some later basket mutation. Not permanently dropped, but not self-correcting.

**4. CONFIRMED — no in-flight guard on row actions.** `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx:142-143`: both `ZimmLink`s call straight through, no disabled or pending state. A fast double-click on Remove issues two `removeItemFromBasket` calls for the same `itemId` (:679, `mutateAsync`, no dedupe) — the second 404s. Same shape for Wishlist → two `createCustomerProductListItem` calls.

**5. PLAUSIBLE — partial state when removal fails after a successful wishlist add.** `attemptMoveToWishlist` awaits `onRemove()` then toasts (:113-115). `removeItem` (:677) doesn't catch, so a rejected removal throws out of the `void attemptMoveToWishlist()` at :137 as an unhandled rejection. Item ends up in the wishlist *and* still in the cart, with no toast and no message.

Checked and clean: `zimmCartDrawer`, `zimmCartEmptyState`, `zimmBenefits`, `zimmCartButtonGroup`, `zimmQuantityStepper`, `cartItemMapper`, `useCartDrawer`. The unmount-orphaned `mutate(…, {onSuccess})` shape appears nowhere else in scope — every cart mutation uses `mutateAsync`.

Out of scope but noted: `moveToWishlist` reads `wishlist` for its already-in-wishlist check too (:709), so that check is equally unreliable at the same moment.</result>

<result>Audited the cart build for performance. Findings ranked by real impact.

**1. `useProducts` for every cart line is not gated on the drawer being open — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:508-511`** (DERIVABLE)
`CartDrawerProvider` renders `CartDrawerContainer` unconditionally (`useCartDrawer.ts:196`), so this mounts on every route. The products query is gated only on `productIds.length > 0`, never on `isOpen`. A shopper with a non-empty basket landing on the homepage fires a full `getProducts` call for their cart contents while LCP is still resolving — content they aren't looking at. React Query caches by key, so it's roughly once per session rather than per route, but the first fire lands on the LCP-critical initial load. Gating with `enabled: isOpen && productIds.length > 0` would cost a short spinner on first open in exchange for removing it from every cold page load. This is the one finding I'd act on.

**2. Context value identity churns on every `_app` render — `useCartDrawer.ts:120`, `_app/index.tsx:203,485`** (DERIVABLE)
`useCartDrawerState` returns a fresh object literal each render, and `onOpen` (line 93) is a new closure each time. Neither is memoised, and the result is passed straight to `CartDrawerProvider value={cartDrawer}`. Every `_app` re-render therefore invalidates the context for all consumers and re-renders `CartDrawerContainer` plus its whole subtree. `useMemo`/`useCallback` here is cheap and contained.

**3. `useIsMutating()` in the container — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:587`** (DERIVABLE)
Subscribes the app-level container to *every* mutation anywhere in the app. Each basket write, wishlist add, or auth mutation re-renders the container on every route. It's deliberate (the comment explains it exists to re-trigger the settle check), but the blast radius is app-wide, not cart-scoped.

**Clean — explicitly not problems:**

- **No N+1.** Line 507 collects all `productId`s into one array and issues a single batched `useProducts` call. `productsById` is properly memoised on `[productsResult]` (518-525).
- **ZimmBenefits' Contentful fetch is correctly scoped.** It's only reachable as `footer` *inside* `ZimmCartDrawer`, and Chakra's Drawer doesn't mount children while closed — so it doesn't fire on non-cart routes. The `<ZimmBenefits />` element is constructed each render (line 766) but that's just an object literal.
- **`useWishList()` at line 674 is free** — `header/index.tsx:152` already calls it app-wide, so it's a deduped cache hit, not a second request.
- **Both polling loops are negligible.** `waitForWishlistReady` (150ms/5s) and `waitForCartWritesToSettle` (80ms/4s) only run during a post-auth resume, are bounded, and amount to a handful of `setTimeout` ticks. Not worth changing.
- **Scroll listener is correctly torn down** (`zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx:141-149`), attached to the element not `window`, keyed on the element via a callback ref, and `scrollAreaContextValue` is memoised (154).
- **Per-row cost is reasonable.** `ZimmCartItemActions` calls `useStyleConfig` + `useIntl` + `useCartMessages` + `usePendingWishlistItem` per row; the last does one `sessionStorage` read per `isGuest` change. Fine at realistic cart sizes.

One thing outside my directive, noted and moved on: `_app` also mounts `useWishlistAuthDrawer` via the container on every route (620), which pulls in `useForm`, three auth helpers and a config read — worth a look, but it's a race/architecture question more than a perf one.</result>

- `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:674,706` — `moveToWishlist` reads `wishlist?.id` from `useWishList()` with no wait, and returns `{status:'error'}` when it's absent

Guest clicks Wishlist on a cart line → signs in → `isGuest` flips → the effect fires in that same commit, when `useWishList()` has just re-keyed to the new customer and is still `undefined` → error branch. The intent is already cleared and `wishlist` isn't a dependency, so nothing retries. content.text:
You're right, and it's worth squaring that properly — because one of these isn't theoretical, we watched it happen today.

---

## Race conditions

**1. Adding to wishlist from the cart doesn't survive signing in.**

*What the shopper sees:* they click Wishlist on a cart row, get asked to sign in, sign in — and nothing happens. Item stays in the cart, never reaches the wishlist, no message explaining why.

*Why:* the app leaves itself a sticky note — "finish this once they're signed in". The instant they sign in, it tears up the note **first**, then tries to do the job. The job needs the shopper's wishlist, which is still loading at that exact moment, so it gives up. The note's already gone, so nothing ever tries again.

*We already saw this.* In the cart-row run earlier today, **no wishlist request was ever sent after login**. I spotted it, said so, and moved past it because you were chasing merge and capping. That observation and this finding are the same thing.

*Fix:* what we did on the product page — wait for the wishlist to actually load, and don't tear up the note until the job's done.

**2. The note can be out of date.** The resumed job can act on an older snapshot of the cart than the one on screen. On its own it's minor; it makes #1 messier.

**3. The quantity cap can go quiet.** If the cap check happens while something else is mid-write, it steps aside — correctly. But nothing schedules another attempt. It only gets retried when the basket changes for some other reason. We watched exactly this today: an over-cap line sat there until a later change nudged it.

**4. Nothing stops a double-click.** Click Remove twice quickly and it sends two delete requests for the same line; the second fails. The buttons never go disabled or pending.

**5. A half-finished move.** If adding to the wishlist succeeds but removing from the cart then fails, the item ends up in both places — no message either way.

---

## Performance

**1. The cart fetches its products on pages you're not looking at.** The cart lives on every page, and it asks for full product details for whatever's in your bag as soon as it can — not when you open the drawer. So a shopper with items in their bag, landing on the homepage, spends part of that first load fetching things they can't see. That lands right where our mobile speed budget is tightest. Fix: only fetch when the drawer actually opens.

**2. More re-drawing than needed.** A small bookkeeping detail makes the cart and everything under it redraw on every app-level update. Cheap, contained fix.

**3. The cart listens to every save anywhere in the app.** Deliberate — it's how it knows when things have settled — but it's a wide net for a cart-shaped problem.

**Genuinely fine, explicitly checked:** it fetches all cart lines in one request, not one per line; the Contentful benefits content only loads when the drawer is open; both waiting loops I added today are trivial; the scroll listener cleans up properly.

---

## Squaring it with "the scenarios work"

They do. Nothing here contradicts that:

- **#1 is the exception** — it's the one scenario that *didn't* work when we ran it, and we chose not to chase it at the time
- **#4 and #5** need a shopper to be fast or unlucky, which scripted runs never are
- **#3** we saw, and it self-healed before it mattered
- **The performance ones break nothing** — they cost speed, which functional testing can't see

So: one real gap in a flow we care about, three edge cases, and one speed item worth taking. Whether any of it belongs in the final part is your call — I've changed nothing.

content.content:
### SFCC-250 — Maximum Purchase Quantity · 9 ACs · 9 of 9 addressed

The rule: **max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order** — CAI-017, `cart.md` §2.
The card states outright it is *not* a component build story: the stepper is 271's, the inline
warning is 795's, the page-level banner is 404's.

| Decision | Value |
|---|---|
| Max value | No BM setting exists (§2.1). Promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant; cart reads the same one. Re-typing `3` would breach `conventions.md`'s no-magic-numbers rule. |
| Threshold | **`>=`**, not the AC's literal "equals" — otherwise a line already holding 4 fails the check and the `+` stays live exactly when it matters. Matches the PDP. |
| Scope of the limit | **Per line item.** Rationale: the SKU is already size *and* colour, so in normal shopping one line **is** one SKU. |
| Merge mode | **`sum_quantities`.** AC5's "combined quantity ... exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. |
| Cap shape | **Consolidate to one line at 3.** Free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single *"merged line item"* for matching products. |
| Merge call | **Zimmermann-owned**, placed where `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — completing the half-implemented pairing in §2.5, and covering all four consumers at once. |
| Callback order | **merge → cap → 272's pending wishlist resume.** The wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing the order moves a quantity the shopper never saw. |
| Render guard | Secondary backstop for baskets that went over some other way (stale session, order-on-behalf). **No-ops while any basket mutation is in flight** via React Query's `useIsMutating()`, so it cannot race the callback. |
| Shared logic | Merge-and-cap lives in **its own small function**, called by both the callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies. |
| Flash (briefly showing 4) | **No action.** Observe the real behaviour first. |
| Loop guard | **Keep it** — distinct from the flash. Without it, a write-on-render can fire repeatedly (concurrent writes racing on one line item; or endless retries if the server refuses), which can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket. One correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error. |

AC disposition: **1, 2** build (needs 271, 795) · **3, 8** → SFCC-404 · **4, 9** nothing to build
(negative assertions; Apple/Google Pay buttons don't exist yet anyway) · **5** build ·
**6, 7** free — they are AC1 and AC2's rules applied to a post-merge state, and a consolidated line
at 3 satisfies per-line `>=`.
